direction: Build configurations incrementally from scratch instead of perturbing the record. Generate several unrelated seeds—random spherical codes, points selected from rescaled $D_9$ root/lattice shells and $E_8\times\mathbb R$ constructions, and greedily selected low-correlation subsets—then grow each from about 150 points to 181 by repeatedly inserting the best of at least 20,000 random deepest-hole candidates and relaxing all points after every five insertions with an annealed hinge or exponential-repulsion objective. Also create variants by deleting 15–25 points from a grown 165-point optimum and regrowing them, which changes the contact graph while retaining a globally distributed frame. Keep internal timing below 155 seconds, evaluate short LP polishes only for the two most promising distinct grown configurations, and return the best; diversity should be measured by pairwise configuration distance after optimal rotation so that near-duplicates of the known record are discarded.

idea: Fresh-basin search with uniform-energy warmup plus sharpening softmax repulsion on many independent random and symmetrized starts, greedy void surgery, and a single short trust-region LP squeeze — avoiding repeated LP basin-hopping that sticks at 0.462474.

Cyclic-shift orbit construction with 20 representatives plus axis fixed point gives 181 points, optimized by annealed softmax repulsion on representatives then broken by graded perturbations and LP polishing.
direction: Search first inside a symmetry-constrained orbit construction and only afterwards break the symmetry. Choose a concrete finite group acting on $\mathbb R^9$, for example signed coordinate permutations generated by cyclic coordinate shifts and sign flips, or a block action of signed permutations preserving a $4+5$ coordinate split, and parameterize a configuration by 8–15 orbit representatives rather than 181 independent points. Optimize the representatives with a smooth max-cosine loss so the full orbit gives at most 181 points, selecting representatives whose orbit sizes sum to 181 or adding one fixed-point orbit on a coordinate axis; then use this highly uniform configuration as a new seed, add perturbations of increasing size from $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-2}$, and LP-polish each perturbed copy. This directly tests whether an approximately group-symmetric, equal-contact structure lies in a better basin than the asymmetric record.

direction: Perform large-scale jammed-core excision with joint, rather than greedy, reinsertion. Repeat with several deletion sizes, such as 8, 14, and 22, because removing only one to four points leaves the old contact topology intact.

direction: Use LP-dual stress to perform targeted core surgery rather than random basin hopping: run one LP polish, extract the dual multipliers for near-maximal pairs from the final LP, compute for each point and contact its dual-weighted stress, then remove the two rattlers plus 10–18 points belonging to the highest-stress connected cluster; with the remaining points temporarily frozen, reinsert the removed points one at a time by optimizing each inserted point against the frozen set using a smooth log-sum-exp objective from at least 200 random starts plus the deepest holes found from 50,000 random sphere samples, then unfreeze everything, apply short exponential-repulsion smoothing, and finish with an LP polish under a strict internal deadline of 155 seconds, returning the incumbent immediately if the deadline is reached.

idea: Target-feasibility continuation on hinge energy with normalized Adam and contact-breaking restarts, lowering tau when feasible and saving LP for the end.
direction: Replace direct minimisation of the nonsmooth maximum by a target-feasibility continuation method: set an aspirational cosine target below the record, such as 0.4615, and minimise the differentiable hinge energy \(\sum_{i<j}\max(0,\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)^4\) plus a small log-sum-exp term using vectorised Adam or L-BFGS on the sphere, starting from the record, random perturbations of it, and configurations generated by deliberately breaking different random subsets of its contacts; whenever a configuration reaches zero hinge energy, lower \(\tau\) by \(2\times10^{-4}\) and continue, otherwise retain the best few configurations by true maximum cosine, and reserve LP polishing only for the final 15 seconds so that many more basin transitions can be tested without repeated LP bottlenecks or timeouts.

direction: Use a lower-$N$ continuation ladder to build a different packing from below: delete 15–25 points (mix of hubs and random points), optimise the remaining 156–166 points hard until their maximum is well below 0.4624, then reinsert points one at a time, each at the deepest of 20000 hole candidates followed by 150 global smoothing steps, with a 1–2 s LP polish after every 4 insertions. Vary the deletion size and random seed across restarts within a 150 s budget, always checkpointing the incumbent, because growing into the available slack lets new points choose their own contact sets instead of inheriting the jammed 181-point graph.

idea: Target-squeeze hinge feasibility with null-space contact slides and final LP polish
direction: Attack the jam directly with a target-squeeze feasibility iteration: fix targets $\tau = \text{best}-2\times10^{-4}, -5\times10^{-4}, -10^{-3}$ in turn and repeatedly solve the linearised problem of minimising total violation $\sum \max(0, \langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)$ over tangent displacements with a large trust radius (0.03–0.08), renormalising after each step, instead of minimising $t$ itself. Interleave null-space slides: compute the Jacobian of the $\sim$1100 active contacts (1100×1448 tangent system), project random tangent noise onto its approximate null space via a few Lanczos/SVD iterations, and step along it to second order so contacts can break and reform without immediately raising the maximum. Keep a hard 150 s deadline, retain the best feasible point found, and finish with a short LP polish.

idea: Independent structured basins with LSE-Adam smoothing plus Hungarian-Procrustes slerp recombination and LP polish.
direction: Generate genuinely independent basins from structured seeds and recombine them correctly: build $\sim$12 starts not derived from the record—random orthogonal-frame unions, permutations of sparse vectors with 2–3 equal nonzero coordinates in $\mathbb{R}^9$, embedded $E_8$-root-like configurations plus a ninth coordinate, and antipodally-biased random codes—optimising each for $\sim$8 s with vectorised log-sum-exp Adam on the sphere ($k$ ramped 80→400). Align the two best distinct outcomes by Hungarian matching on pairwise inner products followed by orthogonal Procrustes alignment, slerp matched point pairs to form a child, then smooth and LP-polish it, all inside a 150 s budget returning the best ever seen. This explores contact topologies unreachable by perturbing the record and tests whether a more symmetric, equitably-contacted arrangement achieves a lower maximum.

idea: Collective core surgery deleting rattlers plus overloaded hubs and random points, reopening holes by relaxing the remainder, greedy deepest-hole reinsertion and exponential-repulsion annealing before short trust-region LP polish under annealing.

Follow with 3–5 s of exponential-repulsion smoothing ($\alpha$ ramped 60→300) and a 3 s LP polish, repeating under a strict 150 s wall-clock deadline that always retains and returns the best configuration ever seen. Accept a cavity result if it beats the incumbent, or with simulated-annealing probability $\exp(-(\text{score}-\text{best})/T)$ for $T$ decaying $10^{-4}\to10^{-6}$, since a cavity this size can genuinely rewire the contact graph.
